description: Evidence sufficiency standards — rules for evaluating whether evidence supports the vulnerability claim. Sourced from review_taxonomy.yaml (EVID) and system_responsibility.md.

entries.title: Evidence sufficient → Confirmed Vulnerability possible
entries.description: When exploitation evidence is present, demonstrates the vulnerability, and includes manual verification, the evidence is sufficient to support classification as Confirmed Vulnerability. However, High/Critical findings still require human confirmation per system_responsibility.md.
entries.action: Evidence is sufficient (EVID_SUFF). Classification can be confirmed_vulnerability. For High/Critical, escalate to human for final approval.

entries.title: Evidence insufficient → Potential Issue required
entries.description: When evidence is present but does not fully demonstrate the vulnerability or lacks manual verification, the evidence is insufficient. The classification MUST be Potential Issue, not Confirmed Vulnerability. Human escalation is recommended.
conditions: vulnerability likely but exploitation not fully demonstrated
OR evidence is insufficient to confirm
entries.action: Evidence is insufficient (EVID_INSUFF). Classification MUST be potential_issue. Recommend human escalation for further verification.

entries.title: No evidence → Potential Issue + mandatory escalation
entries.description: When no exploitation evidence is provided, the finding cannot be confirmed. Classification MUST be Potential Issue and human escalation is mandatory regardless of confidence score.
entries.action: Evidence is absent (EVID_NONE). Classification MUST be potential_issue. Mandatory human escalation — cannot be overridden by confidence score.

entries.title: Scanner output only → Potential Issue + mandatory escalation
entries.description: Scanner output alone is NOT sufficient to confirm a vulnerability. A finding supported only by automated scanner output (without manual verification) MUST be classified as Potential Issue with mandatory human escalation.
entries.action: Evidence is scanner-only (EVID_SCANNER_ONLY). Classification MUST be potential_issue. Mandatory human escalation. Per problem_definition §10: 'Do not treat scanner output alone as proof of a confirmed vulnerability.'

entries.title: Missing reproduction steps flagged but not blocking
entries.description: Findings without reproduction steps are flagged as having incomplete evidence, but this does not block the review. Reproduction steps strengthen evidence but their absence alone does not force Potential Issue classification.
entries.action: Flag as missing reproduction steps (EVID). Reduce evidence_completeness score. Do not force classification change based solely on missing reproduction.

entries.title: Never invent or hallucinate evidence
entries.description: The system must never generate evidence that is not present in the input finding. If evidence is missing, use null or flag as missing. This is a core safety principle from problem_definition §12.
conditions: evidence is missing or insufficient for a claim
entries.action: Do NOT generate synthetic evidence. Use null for missing values. Flag as unsupported claim. Escalate to human if evidence is critical for classification.
